references.text: Psalm 1 describes the blessed man who meditates on the Lord's law day and night, which directly mirrors Joshua's command to meditate on the Book of the Law day and night.
Moses commands that the king shall write a copy of the law and read in it all his days, so that he may learn to fear the Lord and keep all the words of this law.
The command that God's word should be in one's heart and spoken about when sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up reflects the same focus on continuous meditation on the law.
The promise of prosperity and success when keeping the covenant's words corresponds with Joshua's promise of success when he holds fast to the Book of the Law.
The psalmist expresses his love for the law and meditates on it all day, which makes him wiser than his enemies.
Proverbs emphasizes that wisdom and understanding come from holding fast to instruction, leading to life and prosperity.
The blessing upon those who read and keep the words of prophecy in Revelation reflects the same principle of blessing through obedience to God's word.
James exhorts believers to be doers of the word and not merely hearers, and that whoever looks into the perfect law of freedom and holds fast to it will be blessed in what they do.
The command to keep all the statutes and walk in the way the Lord has commanded, so that you may prosper, parallels the promise in Joshua of success through obedience.
Joshua's later command to the tribes to keep the law of Moses and walk in the ways of the Lord repeats the theme from chapter 1.
